chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said one day, while he was delivering a sermon on the pulpit in Kufa: 'O people! If it were not for my aversion to treachery, I would have been the most crafty of people. Indeed, for every act of treachery there is an act of immorality, and for every act of immorality there is an act of disbelief. Indeed, treachery, immorality, and betrayal are in the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between treachery, immorality, and disbelief according to Imam Ali's sermon in Kufa?
ai.summary: In this famous sermon from Kufa, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that his renowned 'cunning' (dahāh) was strategic wisdom rather than deceit, distinguishing his leadership style from the treachery (ghadr) he abhorred. He establishes a theological progression where treachery leads to moral corruption (fujur) and ultimately to disbelief (kufr), a concept deeply explored in Shia exegesis as the path from minor sins to major apostasy. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the spiritual consequences of betrayal in both political and personal contexts within Shia jurisprudence.
